tree: per-tool module split landed; D2/D3 + optional file + read-only handler + byte-read-only T2 measurement
method: charter §6: warm, 5 measured runs after 2 warm-up calls; p50/p95 are nearest-rank over the 5 runs. Default arguments only ({symbol}). BB_NO_AUTO_REFRESH=1 on every measurement. The reference-index tier is measured through the tool's BYTE-READ-ONLY open (`BrainDatabase.getRawInstance(projectId,{readonly:true})`) and the index's own files are sha256-hashed before and after the run. The hub case uses the baseline protocol exactly (1 warm-up + 3 measured handler calls for {"symbol":"getRawInstance"}, budget 5 000 ms) plus an 8-run warm series.

environment.runtime: source tree via npx tsx (no dist build in the measurement path)
environment.note: The machine was running the fleet during every tier and still the fixture and reference tiers are inside budget; the T2 controls and the per-call numbers are the evidence.

tiers.openMode: BrainDatabase.getRawInstance(projectId,{readonly:true}) — the handler opens the same way; no migrations, no healers, no WAL movement
tiers.verdict: inside budget (every measured call p95 <= 327.7 ms)

dbHashProof.note: sha256 of each file identical before and after the whole measurement run; raw hashes in latency-t2-final.json

measurementCorrection.earlierMeasurement: A first campaign pass measured T2 through READ-WRITE opens on a pre-fix planner state and recorded 13.7–359.5 s per default call (join 22.15 s, has 359.53 s, named 100.86 s, computeImpact 23.60 s), and a hand-built comparison attributed the cost to the engine's owner-cascade JOIN form (10 351 ms) against a flat target-indexed form (12.5 ms).
measurementCorrection.whatChanged: The index on disk now carries the owner-range composite index (`brain_symbol_project_owner_idx (project_id, owner_symbol_id)`) and the planner selects it together with `brain_rel_proj_type_target_idx`; reads also open byte-read-only, so no open-path migrations/healers run.
measurementCorrection.remeasurement: On the current index, byte-read-only, the same JOIN form answers in 1.1–1.2 ms and the engine walk in 40–63 ms; the full handler tier is p95 153.6–327.7 ms and the index files are byte-identical after the run.
measurementCorrection.conclusion: T2 is INSIDE budget on the current index, and the earlier multi-second-to-minute figures are retained as the historical evidence for why the owner-range index exists — not as a current product metric.

hubCase.breach: The Lead's common T2 harness measured the default hub call at p50 6337 / p95 6539 ms (budget 5000).
hubCase.diagnosis: NOT the walk (2.0-2.5 s) and not JSON (171 KB serialises in 1 ms): the completeness walk's level query used IN(SELECT … WHERE id IN (...) OR owner-range predicates), which made SQLite abandon the target index. One level-1 batch of 200 measured 4349.5 ms; the same 137 rows via a flat target-id list measured 4.1 ms.
hubCase.fix: the level query is now a flat target-id list (cascade-range members resolved through brain_symbol_project_owner_idx first, relationship query driven by brain_rel_proj_type_target_idx); the walk gets a declared wall deadline (1500 ms) and the component a declared call deadline (3000 ms), both published with declared truncation, a measured total when the measurement ran, and countVerification.skipped when it could not.
hubCase.result: p50 2805 / p95 3148 ms under the baseline protocol; p95 3029 ms over eight warm runs; all declared (truncated=true, walkTimeExhausted=true, total 406 or skipped for the deadline), index byte-identical after.
